title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Recognition, Assessment and Shared-Care Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition and referral of possible ADHD, plus monitoring within an agreed specialist-led shared-care plan.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting attention, activity and impulse control. Impairment varies across settings and developmental stages. Sleep, learning, mood, autism and environmental adversity can mimic or coexist with ADHD.
keyMechanisms: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting attention, activity and impulse control.
Impairment varies across settings and developmental stages.
Sleep, learning, mood, autism and environmental adversity can mimic or coexist with ADHD.

references.title: NICE NG87: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder—diagnosis and management

symptoms: Persistent inattention, hyperactivity and/or impulsivity causing functional difficulty.
physicalSigns: School, work, relationship or daily-living impairment across more than one setting.
redFlags: Self-harm risk, psychosis, mania, severe aggression, safeguarding concern or dangerous substance use requires urgent parallel assessment.
precipitants: Demands exceeding executive-function capacity, sleep deprivation and inconsistent treatment can expose or worsen impairment.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Persistent social-communication differences and restricted or repetitive behaviours.
Mood or worry pattern better explains concentration change.
Daytime symptoms track inadequate or disrupted sleep.
Difficulties are concentrated around specific developmental or academic tasks.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: A trained specialist makes the diagnosis from a full clinical and psychosocial assessment, developmental and psychiatric history, observer reports and diagnostic criteria; rating scales alone are insufficient (NG87 1.3).

ruleIn.normalValue: Age-appropriate attention, activity and impulse control
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Persistent symptoms causing impairment in more than one important setting
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Diagnosis requires a full clinical and psychosocial assessment; rating scales alone are insufficient.

ruleIn.normalValue: Scores below validated concern thresholds with no cross-setting impairment
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Concordant functional impairment reported by home and education or work
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports but does not replace clinical diagnosis.

ruleIn.normalValue: No alternative disorder or high-risk substance pattern explaining symptoms
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Coexisting or alternative neurodevelopmental, mood, sleep or substance-use condition
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Changes the treatment plan and urgency.

ruleIn.normalValue: No neurological, thyroid or dysmorphic abnormality
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Findings suggesting another diagnosis or comorbidity
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Direct targeted investigation or referral rather than routine broad testing.

ruleIn.normalValue: Tracking expected age- and sex-adjusted centiles
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Growth faltering, weight loss or obesity
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record before medicine and monitor during treatment.

ruleIn.normalValue: Within age-appropriate centiles or adult reference range
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record before medicine; seek specialist advice for significant abnormalities.

ruleOut.normalValue: No exertional syncope, concerning family history, murmur or heart-failure sign
ruleOut.expectedFinding: A concerning symptom, family history or examination finding
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Obtain cardiology advice before stimulant treatment when indicated.

ruleOut.normalValue: Sinus rhythm with intervals in the age-appropriate range
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Not routine when cardiovascular history and examination are normal; use for a clinical indication.

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and support
actions: Document duration, settings, functional impact, development, sleep, mental health, substance use and safeguarding.
Offer environmental and parent/carer support while awaiting assessment; support need not wait for diagnosis.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for specialist assessment
clinicalManagement.timeframe: When symptoms persist with at least moderate impairment
actions: Send school or workplace information and relevant physical/mental-health history.
Use urgent mental-health or safeguarding pathways for immediate risk.

clinicalManagement.title: Operate shared care only by agreement
actions: Prescribe and monitor only under a documented shared-care arrangement that names responsibilities.
Escalate adverse effects, poor response, misuse/diversion concern or diagnostic uncertainty to the specialist.

medicationPlan.note: Initiation and titration remain specialist-led. Use modified-release products exactly as prescribed; formulations are not automatically interchangeable. Current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.

regimens.patientGroup: Child aged 5 years or over or young person
regimens.duration: Titrate to response; maximum 54 mg daily for children on the cited Concerta XL label
adjustments: Titrate against symptoms and adverse effects under specialist supervision.
Swallow modified-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
No specific renal or hepatic dosing recommendation is established in the cited label; specialist/pharmacy review is required.
Check hospital formulary; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Height every 6 months; weight at the age-specific intervals in NICE NG87 Recommendation 1.8.5.
Pulse and blood pressure before and after each dose change and every 6 months.
Appetite, sleep, behaviour, tics and misuse/diversion risk.
contraindications: Severe cardiovascular disease, severe hypertension, glaucoma, phaeochromocytoma, hyperthyroidism or thyrotoxicosis.
Current monoamine-oxidase inhibitor use or use within 14 days.
Specialist review for psychosis, mania, seizures or significant substance-use risk.

teaching.scope: Recognition and referral of possible ADHD, plus monitoring within an agreed specialist-led shared-care plan.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Self-harm risk, psychosis, mania, severe aggression, safeguarding concern or dangerous substance use requires urgent parallel assessment.
Prescribe and monitor only under a documented shared-care arrangement that names responsibilities.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: No acute risk; referral or shared-care responsibility is explicit; family/patient knows whom to contact.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: At each review assess benefit, adverse effects, growth/vitals where relevant, adherence, sleep, functioning and ongoing need for treatment.
